title: Hawkish Fed Repricing Revives Hike Risk, Lifting the Dollar and Front-End Yields
content:
The window's defining shift was markets abandoning their dovish framing as sticky inflation and firm data revived the prospect of a Fed hike, not a cut. July CPI held at **3.4%** year-on-year with core near 2.5%, keeping prices above target, and Chair Warsh used Jackson Hole to own the inflation record and call financial conditions 'not restrictive'.

Momentum built when August payrolls smashed forecasts at **162,000** against expectations near 55,000, with unemployment steady at 4.1%. Fed funds futures swung to price roughly a **60%** chance of a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC, lifting the 2-year yield to its highest since early 2025 near **4.39%** and driving pronounced **bear-flattening**; the dollar rallied to a multi-week high.

Late dovish pushback from Governor Waller trimmed hike odds towards 50%, leaving a two-way market into the meeting. The repricing rippled across rates, FX and equities, making every inflation and jobs print pivotal.

title: AI Earnings Drive Equities to Records Before Rate Fears Spark a Pullback
content:
US equities' engine stayed the AI complex, which powered indices to fresh records through the window. The S&P 500 struck an intraday peak near **7,814.88** and logged its strongest week since April, with semiconductors leading the advance and breadth still narrow.

Nvidia's late-August results anchored the run: earnings up roughly **109%** and data-centre revenue climbing **92%** to about $25bn underscored relentless **AI capex** from cloud and enterprise buyers, dragging Micron and Marvell higher alongside.

The rally stalled into month-end as the hawkish rate repricing lifted yields and the dollar, pulling the S&P back toward 7,720 and the Nasdaq off its highs, while a sharp Lululemon miss flagged consumer caution. The clash between AI-driven earnings strength and richer discount rates left tech leadership the decisive swing factor for broad indices.

title: Precious Metals Stall as Firmer Dollar and Real Yields Cool the Debasement Trade
content:
After leading earlier windows, precious metals lost momentum as the hawkish turn firmed the dollar and lifted **real yields**, undercutting the **debasement hedge** narrative. Bullion slid from its highs to a near one-month low around **$4,470** by early September.

The correction tracked the Fed repricing: as hike odds climbed after Jackson Hole and the strong payrolls print, the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding metal rose while the dollar posted its best week in seven months. Gold pared losses only when Governor Waller's dovish remarks nudged hike bets lower, recovering towards **$4,500**.

The episode showed metals remain hostage to the rate and currency path rather than a one-way store-of-value bid. With the September FOMC and fresh inflation data ahead, gold and silver stayed a sensitive barometer of real-rate and dollar direction.
